title: A balanced 13-variable Boolean function with absolute indicator 112
abstract: We exhibit an explicit balanced Boolean function $f\colon\F_2^{13}\to\F_2$ of algebraic degree $11$ whose absolute indicator is $\Delta_f=\max_{d\neq 0}\bigl|\sum_{x}(-1)^{f(x)\oplus f(x\oplus d)}\bigr|=112$. Since $112<2^{\lfloor (13+1)/2\rfloor}=128$, this is a counterexample to the conjecture of Zhang and Zheng (1995) in the case $n=13$; to our knowledge, for odd $n$ the conjecture had previously been disproved only for $n\in\{9,11,15,21\}$. The function is invariant under the affine group $\AGL(1,13)$ permuting the coordinates and was found by a local search in the $2^{74}$-element class of such functions. Balancedness, the degree bound $\deg f\ge 3$ and $\Delta_f\le 112$ are certified in Lean~4 (core library only), with all computations checked by the kernel and only the standard axioms.

title: An explicit 6-regular graph of girth 9 on 4368 vertices
abstract: We construct an explicit $6$-regular simple graph of girth exactly $9$ on $4368$ vertices. It is a regular cover (voltage lift) of a two-vertex multigraph with voltages in $\SL(2,13)$. Consequently $n(6,9)\le 4368$, where $n(k,g)$ is the order of a $(k,g)$-cage. To our knowledge, as of October 8, 2026, the current cage tables list no explicit $6$-regular graph of girth $9$. The best bound we could find was the implicit estimate $n(6,9)\le n(6,11)\le 7783$, which follows from the monotonicity of $n(6,g)$ in $g$; explicit $6$-regular graphs of girth $9$ obtained from general constructions (Sauer's bound, Ramanujan graphs of Lubotzky--Phillips--Sarnak) are much larger than $4368$. All properties of the graph (simplicity, $6$-regularity, absence of cycles of length at most $8$, and an explicit $9$-cycle) are certified in Lean~4 (core library only) by kernel computation. The proof uses only the standard axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and \texttt{Quot.sound}. The lower bound $n(6,9)\ge 938$ is unchanged, so a large gap remains.

title: Explicit lower bounds for runs of three consecutive\\ quintic and septic residues
abstract: For a prime $p$ let $r(k,3,p)$ be the least $r\ge1$ such that $r,r+1,r+2$ are all $k$-th power residues modulo $p$, and $\Lambda(k,3)=\limsup_{p\to\infty}r(k,3,p)$. Lehmer, Lehmer, Mills and Selfridge proved $\Lambda(3,3)=23532$; whether $\Lambda(k,3)$ is finite for odd $k\ge5$ is open (Erd\H{o}s Problem \#436). We give explicit assignments of quintic (resp.\ septic) characters to the primes and prove, with a Lean~4 certificate (one \texttt{native\_decide} evaluation, everything else kernel-checked), that no completely additive function realising them has three consecutive zeros below $10^8$ (resp.\ $10^7$). Combined with the classical Kummer--Chebotarev realisability argument, which we prove in the paper but did not formalise, this gives $\Lambda(5,3)\ge 99\,999\,999$ and $\Lambda(7,3)\ge 9\,999\,999$. Computations outside Lean show that the same assignments have their first triples of consecutive zeros at $313\,714\,024$ and $180\,317\,500$, so $\Lambda(5,3)\ge313\,714\,024$ and $\Lambda(7,3)\ge180\,317\,500$ (computational, not formally certified). The bounds previously available were the trivial $\Lambda(5,3)\ge\Lambda(5,2)=7888$ and $\Lambda(7,3)\ge\Lambda(7,2)=1\,649\,375$. Whether $\Lambda(5,3)$ and $\Lambda(7,3)$ are finite remains open.

title: New four-dimensional linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_8$ and $\mathbb{F}_9$ improving Maruta's tables
abstract: Let $n_q(4,d)$ be the smallest length of a linear $[n,4,d]_q$ code. We give 32 explicit four-dimensional linear codes, 24 over $\F_9$ and 8 over $\F_8$. Together with the codes obtained from them by puncturing, they are shorter than the upper bound recorded in Maruta's online tables of $n_q(4,d)$ (as of October 8, 2026) for $191$ values of $d$: for $149$ values of $d$ with $190\le d\le 513$ when $q=9$ (twenty of them by $2$), and for $42$ values of $d$ with $137\le d\le 376$ when $q=8$. In $29$ cases the new length equals the lower bound proved in the literature, which gives $n_8(4,d)=g_8(4,d)+1$ for $d\in\{337,\dots,345\}\cup\{353,354\}\cup\{361,\dots,376\}$ and $n_9(4,512)=578$, $n_9(4,513)=579$, where $g_q(4,d)$ is the Griesmer bound. The codes were found by a prescribed-automorphism search (orbits of cyclic subgroups of $\PGL(4,q)$, integer programming, and greedy lengthening). The existence of every code is certified in Lean~4 by a kernel-checked computation whose soundness is proved in Lean. The lower bounds are cited, not re-proved.

title: New lower bounds for line-free sets in $\mathbb{F}_7^3$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$
abstract: A subset of $\F_p^n$ is \emph{line-free} if it contains no affine line, equivalently no $p$-term arithmetic progression with nonzero common difference; $r_p(\F_p^n)$ denotes the largest size of such a set. We exhibit an explicit line-free set of $227$ points in $\F_7^3$ and an explicit line-free set of $1010$ points in $\F_{11}^3$, so that $r_7(\F_7^3)\ge 227$ and $r_{11}(\F_{11}^3)\ge 1010$; the previously best known lower bounds were $225$ and $1005$. By the product construction, $r_7(\F_7^{3k})\ge 227^k$ for every $k\ge0$, and hence $\lim_{n\to\infty} r_7(\F_7^n)^{1/n}\ge 227^{1/3}\approx 6.1002$; this improves the three-dimensional product bound $225^{1/3}\approx 6.0822$ of Elsholtz et al., but not the best known bound $7^{20/21}\approx 6.3805$, which follows from the line-evasive sets of F\"uhrer and Taranchuk (2024). The sets were found by tabu search with iterated local search. Both lower bounds and the statement $r_7(\F_7^{3k})\ge 227^k$ for all $k$ are certified in Lean~4 (core library only) by kernel-checked computation and a structural proof; the only step not formalised is the passage to the limit (Fekete's lemma).

title: New lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers\\ from composite cyclic moduli
abstract: Let $\W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. We give explicit colourings showing $\W(4,6)>255{,}606$, $\W(5,6)>1{,}278{,}030$, $\W(6,6)>2{,}531{,}178$, $\W(4,8)>18{,}874{,}790$, $\W(4,9)>212{,}844{,}870$, $\W(5,10)>13{,}086{,}046{,}358$, $\W(4,11)>3{,}761{,}291{,}754$, $\W(4,12)>37{,}088{,}321{,}982$ and seven further bounds for five and six colours (\cref{tab:main}). To our knowledge, as of October 8, 2026, these improve fifteen entries of the standard tables (the Wikipedia table of $\W(r,k)$ and Monroe's table of four-colour bounds). No new search is involved. The colourings come from one elementary blow-up lemma applied to cyclic $2$- and $3$-colourings that are already in the literature (Rabung; Herwig--Heule--van~Lambalgen--van~Maaren; Rabung--Lotts; Heule; cf.\ Kouril--Paul for $\W(2,6)$). These certificates are cyclic on \emph{composite} moduli ($226$, $1642$, $5158$, $19394$, $58066$) that exceed the prime moduli used in the published product bounds. We also use the Blankenship--Cummings--Taranchuk block step with the prime $p=11>k$ for $k=10$, as their own remark allows. Every bound is certified by a kernel-checked proof in Lean~4 (core only, no Mathlib) whose main theorems depend only on the standard axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, \texttt{Quot.sound}.

title: New proper circulant weighing matrices\\ from a twin of the Singer construction
abstract: A circulant weighing matrix $\CW(n,k)$ is a circulant $n\times n$ matrix $W$ with entries in $\{0,\pm1\}$ and $WW^{\mathsf T}=kI$; it is proper if it is not the lift of a smaller one. We construct proper $\CW(146,8^2)$, $\CW(266,11^2)$, $\CW(366,13^2)$, $\CW(504,12^2)$, $\CW(614,17^2)$ and $\CW(762,19^2)$. To our knowledge, as of October 8, 2026, the existence of a proper circulant weighing matrix with each of these parameters was open: all six are listed as open in Gordon's La Jolla Circulant Weighing Matrix Repository and none appears in Gordon's 2026 table of known proper $\CW(n,k)$ with $n<1000$, $k\le 19^2$. For $\CW(504,144)$ no circulant weighing matrix of any kind was known. All six first rows are explicit and are verified in Lean~4 (core library only) by kernel evaluation. Four of them come from a new ``twin'' of the classical Singer-complement construction. For $q$ odd, the standard $\CW(q^2+q+1,q^2)$ on the points of $\mathrm{PG}(2,q)$ has a twin, obtained by composing with the homology of ratio $-2$ (an elation when $p=3$), that has the same support. Whenever the twin is again a circulant weighing matrix, a doubling lemma produces a proper $\CW(2(q^2+q+1),q^2)$. We conjecture that this holds for every odd prime power $q$. It has been checked by computer for all odd prime powers $q\le251$, but we have no proof. The other two matrices come from a multiplier-restricted search ($n=146$) and from a product over non-coprime orders ($n=504$).

title: Proof of Sun's conjecture on coprime adjacent sums\\ (OEIS A228886)
abstract: For $n\ge 1$ let $a(n)$ be the number of permutations $(i_0,i_1,\dots,i_n)$ of $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$ with $i_0=0$ and $i_n=n$ such that all $n+1$ cyclic adjacent sums $i_0+i_1,\ i_1+i_2,\ \dots,\ i_{n-1}+i_n,\ i_n+i_0$ are coprime to both $n-1$ and $n+1$ (OEIS A228886). In 2013 Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured that $a(n)>0$ for every $n\ge1$ except $n=2,4$, and proved this for odd $n$. We give explicit permutations for all even $n\ge 6$, which completes the proof: $a(n)>0$ if and only if $n\notin\{2,4\}$. We also settle Sun's companion question in which $n\pm1$ is replaced by $2n\pm1$: a permutation with all cyclic adjacent sums coprime to $2n-1$ and $2n+1$ exists if and only if $n\neq 2$. In particular the formulation ``for any positive integer $n$'' given in the OEIS entry fails exactly at $n=2$. Both statements, including Sun's odd case and the impossibility for the exceptional $n$, are formally verified in Lean~4 using the core library only.

title: Settling small open cases of signed difference sets
abstract: A $(v,k,\lambda)$ signed difference set in a finite abelian group $G$ of order $v$ is a group-ring element $D=\sum_g s_g g$ with $s_g\in\{-1,0,1\}$, exactly $k$ nonzero coefficients, and $DD^{(-1)}=(k-\lambda)1_G+\lambda G$. Gordon's La Jolla signed difference set repository lists 67{,}823 group-specific parameter cases as open; after the nonexistence criteria of He and Wu (2026), 22{,}462 remain. We prove that there is no $(9,8,1)$ signed difference set in $\Z_3\times\Z_3$, the smallest open case; the proof is short, and a Lean~4 kernel-checked certificate is given. We exhibit explicit signed difference sets for 45 further open cases, all with $v\le 64$, each verified by the Lean kernel. To our knowledge, as of October 8, 2026, 26 of these are new. These include an eighth-order cyclotomic $(25,12,1)$ signed difference set in $\GF(25)$ and examples in $\Z_3\times\Z_9$, in six groups of order 32, and in seven groups of order 64. Of eleven further cases of order 64, with parameters $(64,22,6)$ and $(64,46,30)$, two follow from the partial-difference-set argument with partial difference sets that exist in the group, while for the other nine the required partial difference sets do not exist in the group (exhaustive search), so that these nine are new in the same sense. Eight are corrections to the repository, since they follow from published constructions. Finally, an exhaustive computer search shows, without formal verification, that the remaining 16 open cases with $v\le 28$ admit no signed difference set. Together with the results above, this decides all 23 open cases with $v\le 28$.

title: Simple polygons whose sides lie on $n$ lines:\\ a parity obstruction and constructions
abstract: Let $M(n)$ be the largest number of sides of a simple polygon all of whose sides lie on $n$ lines. A closed-trail argument gives $M(n)\le n\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$, and it was asked on MathOverflow whether equality always holds. For odd $n=2r+1$ we prove two things. First, in every simple arrangement of $n$ pseudolines, a certain $2$-regular graph on the intersection points, the alternating $2$-factor, has a number of components congruent to $(n^2-1)/8 \pmod 2$. Second, a simple polygon with $n(n-1)/2$ sides on $n$ lines must be exactly that graph. Consequently, if $n\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$ then $M(n)\le n(n-1)/2-3$; in particular the conjectured equality fails for $n=7,9,15,17,\dots$. The proof of the parity statement is elementary: a sweep of the wiring diagram and a potential function on permutations. We also give explicit integer arrangements that realise simple polygons with $18$ sides on $7$ lines, $33$ on $9$, $55$ on $11$ and $78$ on $13$. Hence $M(7)=18$ and $M(9)=33$, while $M(11)=55$ and $M(13)=78$ attain the bound. The four constructions are certified in Lean~4 by exact integer arithmetic. The parity theorem and the upper bounds are proved on paper only; they are confirmed by exhaustive computation over all simple arrangements of at most $9$ pseudolines, but are not formally verified.

title: A kissing configuration of 12\,277 points in dimension 19
abstract: We exhibit $12\,277$ points on the unit sphere $S^{18}\subset\R^{19}$ with pairwise angular distances at least $60^\circ$. Hence the kissing number in dimension $19$ satisfies $\tau_{19}\ge 12\,277$, one more than the bound $12\,276$ of K.~Li (October 2026). The configuration keeps Li's $10\,484$-point base, which comes from the odd-sign configuration of Cohn and Li. It restores one more of the $184$ base points that Li deletes, and it replaces Li's $1792$ added points by $1792$ re-optimised points. These form $112$ orbits under the order-$16$ group of sign changes that fixes the restored point. All coordinates are integers. Every pair is checked in exact arithmetic by two independent programs. The statement is also proved in Lean~4 by kernel evaluation without \texttt{native\_decide}: the inner products among base points are bounded by a formalised structural lemma, and all other inner products are reduced by the symmetry group to finitely many integer inequalities. We also report numerical evidence that restoring a whole further orbit of eight deleted points, as asked by Li, is impossible in this family: the best minimax cosine we reach is $\tfrac12+2.0\cdot10^{-5}$.

title: A new lower bound for the cap set capacity
abstract: Let $C=\lim_{n\to\infty} r_3(\F_3^n)^{1/n}$ be the cap set capacity, where $r_3(\F_3^n)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\F_3^n$ without three distinct points on a line. We show $C> \NLEAN$; the explicit construction gives $C\ge\NBOUND$. This improves the bound $2.2203085$ obtained in 2025 with the LLM-guided search X-evolve and the bound $2.2202337$ of FunSearch (2023). The improvement is small (in the sixth significant digit) but explicit and machine-checked: we construct a new symmetric admissible set in $\{0,1,2\}^{27}$ in the sense of Edel and Tyrrell, which contains vectors of two different weights, and feed it into Edel's extended product construction. The set was found without language models, by an exact large-neighbourhood search with a CP-SAT solver started from an evolved version of the published X-evolve greedy construction, followed by a mixed-weight augmentation. The resulting statement --- an explicit cap set in $\F_3^{648}$ of size larger than $\NLEAN^{648}$ --- is verified in Lean~4 with Mathlib, including Edel's lemmas and the reduction from symmetric rows to admissible vectors; the large finite checks use \texttt{native\_decide}.

title: An improved upper bound for binary covering codes\\ of length 20 and covering radius 3
abstract: Let $K(n,R)$ denote the minimum number of words in a binary code of length $n$ with covering radius $R$. We show $K(20,3)\le 1984$, improving the bound $K(20,3)\le 2048$ recorded in Kéri's standard tables of covering codes. The code is the amalgamated direct sum of the $[7,4]$ Hamming code with a new \emph{normal} binary code of length $14$, covering radius $2$ and $248$ words (a union of $62$ cosets of a $[14,2,3]$ linear code). The covering property is certified in Lean~4 with Mathlib, using only the standard axioms. We also report, as negative results, extensive but unsuccessful computer searches aimed at the football pool problem $K_3(n,1)$ for $n=6,7,8$.

title: Mod-4 obstructions for completing the rank-47 $\F_2$ algorithms\\ for $4\times 4$ matrix multiplication
abstract: The best known bilinear algorithms for multiplying two $4\times4$ matrices use $47$ multiplications over fields of characteristic two (AlphaTensor, 2022; Kauers--Moosbauer, 2023) and $48$ multiplications over rings containing $\tfrac12$ (AlphaEvolve, 2025; Dumas--Pernet--Sedoglavic, 2025), while every known algorithm that is valid over all rings, for instance over $\Z/2^{64}\Z$, uses $49$. It is known that the two rank-$47$ schemes over $\F_2$ do not lift to characteristic zero. We show that they cannot be completed to rank-$48$ schemes over $\Z/4\Z$ either: there is no decomposition of the $4\times4\times4$ matrix multiplication tensor over $\Z/4\Z$ (hence none over $\Z$ or over the $2$-adic integers) consisting of $48$ rank-one terms of which $47$ reduce modulo $2$ to the AlphaTensor scheme and the remaining one vanishes modulo $2$. More generally, no correction of the form $2\,x\otimes M$, with an arbitrary $16\times16$ block $M$, can repair the mod-$4$ defect of the lifted scheme. The proof reduces the question to linear algebra over $\F_2$ and is certified by $1585$ explicit linear functionals. The reduction is formalised in Lean~4 with Mathlib; the finite checks on the explicit certificate are run with \texttt{native\_decide}; the link between the data and the matrix multiplication tensor is kernel-checked. The same statement holds, with its own certificate and the same formalisation, for the Kauers--Moosbauer scheme. Both schemes are rigid in the flip graph: an exhaustive exploration through rank $48$ (flips, plus transitions, reductions) reaches no other scheme of rank $\le47$. We also report the analogous computation for the rank-$73$ $\F_2$ scheme of $\langle 4,5,5\rangle$ and $2$-adic integrality measurements for several rational records.

title: New best-known configurations for Heilbronn's triangle problem\\ in a triangle with $23$ and $35$ points
abstract: For a triangle $T$ of unit area let $\Hn(n)$ be the largest possible value of the smallest area of a triangle spanned by $n$ points of $T$. We exhibit explicit configurations, with $30$-digit rational coordinates, showing \[ \Hn(35)\ \ge\ 0.0042542724\ldots \qquad\text{and}\qquad \Hn(23)\ \ge\ 0.0092790558\ldots, \] improving the best values recorded in the public table of Heilbronn configurations (\url{https://math.tejstead.com/heilbronn}) at the time of writing, $0.0041984701\ldots$ and $0.0092756410\ldots$ (both due to N.~Sudermann-Merx, October 2026), by $1.33\%$ and $0.037\%$. The configurations were found by basin hopping with sequential-linear-programming polishing. Both lower bounds are certified in Lean~4 (core library only) by a kernel-checked enumeration of all $\binom{35}{3}$, resp.\ $\binom{23}{3}$, triangles in exact rational arithmetic. Nothing is claimed about optimality.

title: New certified upper bounds for the sign-uncertainty constant and the first autocorrelation constant
abstract: We prove two new upper bounds for constants from the AlphaEvolve benchmark collection, both with certificates checked by the kernel of the Lean~4 proof assistant (with Mathlib, no \texttt{native\_decide}, only the standard axioms). (1) For the one-dimensional sign-uncertainty constant of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane, $C_{\mathrm{SU}}\le 0.305578$, improving the previous record $0.3089$ (and the published bound $0.3216$); the witness is $f(x)=P(2\pi x^2)e^{-\pi x^2}$ with $P$ an explicit integer combination of the Laguerre polynomials $L_{2j}^{(-1/2)}$, $j\le 300$. Lean verifies the sign pattern of $P$ exactly; the reduction from the sign pattern to the bound is the classical Hermite eigenfunction argument. (2) For the first autocorrelation (Sidon) constant, $C_1\le 1.5027434864131$, improving the previous record $1.502743486709583$ by $3\cdot10^{-10}$; here the continuous statement, including the definition of $C_1$, is formalised. The kernel checks rely on Kronecker substitution: all coefficients needed by the certificates are read off as base-$2^w$ digits of a few very large integers, which the Lean kernel multiplies with GMP.

title: New lower bounds for hypergraph Ramsey numbers\\ from affine-invariant colourings
abstract: We prove \[ R(4,5;3)\ge 38,\quad R(5,5;3)\ge 98,\quad R(4,6;3)\ge 68,\quad R(5,5;4)\ge 38,\quad R(5,6;4)\ge \RFSF, \] improving the lower bounds $35$, $88$, $63$, $35$ and $67$ listed in revision~\#18 (April 2026) of Radziszowski's dynamic survey \emph{Small Ramsey Numbers}. Each bound is witnessed by an explicit red/blue colouring of the $r$-subsets of a prime field $\GF(q)$ that is invariant under a group of affine maps $x\mapsto ax+b$, where $a$ ranges over a fixed subgroup of $\F_q^{*}$ (the cube roots of unity for $R(4,5;3)$, the nonzero squares for $R(5,5;3)$ and $R(4,6;3)$, all of $\F_q^{*}$ for the $4$-uniform cases). Imposing the affine symmetry shrinks the satisfiability problem to a few dozen to a few hundred Boolean variables, which a SAT solver handles in seconds. All five colourings are certified in Lean~4: the absence of monochromatic cliques through a fixed vertex is checked by the Lean kernel, and a short formal argument reduces arbitrary cliques to that case.

title: Symmetric Hadamard matrices of orders 532 and 732
abstract: We construct symmetric Hadamard matrices of orders $532=4\cdot133$ and $732=4\cdot183$. To our knowledge these are the first symmetric Hadamard matrices of these orders: $v=133$ and $v=183$ appear in the most recent published list of odd $v<200$ for which no symmetric Hadamard matrix of order $4v$ was known. Both come from the propus construction applied to cyclic difference families whose blocks are unions of orbits of a multiplier subgroup: parameters $(133;61,64,64,57;113)$ with the subgroup $\langle26\rangle$ of order $6$ in $\Z_{133}^{*}$, and $(183;81,91,91,83;163)$ with the subgroup $\langle34\rangle$ of order $5$ in $\Z_{183}^{*}$. The second family was found with a compression-guided exhaustive search exploiting $183=3\cdot61$. Both existence statements are formally verified in Lean~4 with Mathlib: we prove the propus construction in general and check the required autocorrelation identities by kernel evaluation. We also report (computational, not formally verified) negative evidence for the smallest open order $260=4\cdot65$: no cyclic propus difference family in $\Z_{65}$ admits a nontrivial multiplier.

title: The best constant in Smale's mean value problem exceeds $1.048$
abstract: For a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d\ge 2$ and a point $z$ with $p'(z)\neq0$ let $R(p,z)=\min_{p'(c)=0}|p(z)-p(c)|/(|z-c|\,|p'(z)|)$, and let $K_d=\sup R(p,z)$ over polynomials of degree $d$. Smale (1981) proved $K_d\le4$ and conjectured $K_d\le1$ (strong form $K_d=(d-1)/d$). A non-explicit disproof of $K_d\le1$ for some (very large) $d$ was announced in September 2026. We prove that $K_d$ is non-decreasing and that $\lim_{d\to\infty}K_d\ge1.048$; thus no constant below $1.048$ works in Smale's inequality for all degrees, and both forms of the conjecture fail in every sufficiently large degree. The proof has two parts. (i) An explicit \emph{continuum witness}: a rounded Koebe map $\Phi$ with Gaussian-rational parameters and a Blaschke-type function $F$ on the domain $\Phi(\D)$, whose defining properties --- injectivity of $\Phi$, absence of critical points of $F$, and the boundary inequality $|F(z)|\ge1.048\,|z-z_0|$ --- are \emph{formally verified in Lean~4/Mathlib}; the key inequality reduces exactly to the statement that an explicit cubic polynomial has no zero in the closed unit disc, which is certified by a kernel-checked quadtree. (ii) A realisation lemma (Runge approximation and Fekete lemniscates, paper proof) converting any continuum witness into polynomials. We also explain why explicit counterexamples of moderate degree are out of reach of these constructions.
